fix: and with this provide three months’ pay for the army, and add tens of thousands of measures of grain.
reason: δοῦσι…μισθοδοτῆσαι: the fifty talents are the three months’ pay. μυριάδας has no numeral; ‘ten thousand’ is supplied. Editor must decide on a numeral.

fix: At this time Aristophantus the general arrived
reason: Greek Ἀριστόφαντος, the Acarnanian strategos, not Aristophanes.

fix: they immediately burst into Thermus and pressed hard on the last men in the column
reason: ἐπέβαλον εἰς τὸν Θέρμον: they broke into Thermus, which Philip had just left. They did not attack from it.
Παλαιεῖς are the people of Pale in Cephallenia, not Palairos. Uses the book’s existing spelling ‘Paleis’ (chs. 3, 26).

fix: crossed the gulf, and as soon as he had anchored at Leucas he instructed the officers
reason: ὡς θᾶττον…καθωρμίσθη is temporal, ‘as soon as he anchored’, not ‘anchored as quickly as possible’.

fix: about two stades from the city
reason: μάλιστα with a numeral means ‘about’, not ‘at most’.
τῆς ὥρας συναγούσης means it was growing late in the day. It explains the forced halt, so ‘day drawing on’ is correct.

fix: promising that the Aetolians would do everything required to conclude the peace
reason: τοὺς Αἰτωλούς is the subject of ποιήσειν. The Aetolians themselves would do everything; the envoys do not bring them round.

fix: The Aetolians, for their part, were eager to conclude peace
reason: The clause ‘hoping to exploit the situation’ has no basis in the Greek. τὰ μὲν ἔσπευδον is answered by ἅμα δὲ…παρεῖλκον.
εἰς ἱμάτιον… is corrupt/gapped; ‘to his quarters’ is invented. Marked [...] per convention; editors read e.g. Apamea or private life.

fix: intending to launch his attack from higher ground
reason: ἐξ ὑπερδεξίου means from a commanding height. ‘On the right’ is a hyperliteral addition.

fix: while above it lie some parts of the Pontus, in the region beyond the Phasis, and it stretches to the Hyrcanian Sea
reason: τινὰ μέρη τοῦ Πόντου is the subject of ὑπέρκειται: parts of the Pontus lie above the territory. Original tail kept.
